exposure: compression due to enlarged uterus in late pregnancy
cohort: The study included 145 pregnant women diagnosed with ovarian endometrioma in the first trimester at a tertiary institute.
finding: Approximately two-thirds (68%) of ovarian endometriomas decreased in size during pregnancy (40% disappeared), 27% remained unchanged, and 5% increased in size, while 2.8% experienced rupture, with adhesions, increased cyst size, large initial size (>=6 cm), and uterine compression identified as related factors.
followup_time: from the first trimester to the postdelivery period
